messages.subject: Query regarding latest idea discussion for GSOC '13
parts:
hello everyone,

I am Pulkit Mehrotra. I am a 4th year  student at IIT Kharagpur doing my Masters in Financial Engineering. I have started working  on R last year during my summer Internship and was amazed by the scope and ease of functionality of the language for financial computation. I have done few projects in finance and am interested in learning and contributing  to R.

I am looking forward to applying to GSOC this year . Is there any place where the ideas regarding the current GSOC are being discussed or list which the current aspirants can go though before applying for a new idea. I didn't find any page on rwiki.scieviews.org where such ideas are being discussed. Is this the main place where the idea discussion shall take place ?

Thank you for your time and consideration. 
Hoping for R being accepted this GSOC :)

best regards,
Pulkit Mehrotra

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: Query regarding latest idea discussion for GSOC '13
parts:
The wiki page for project ideas is here:

http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2013

All prospective mentors should be posting project outlines there.  Students who wish to participate may feel free to start communicating with the mentors.  I'd expect more projects to get filled in over the next several weeks.

If a student is proposing a project, and is looking for a mentor, then the project outline should clearly state that it is a student proposed project, and strive to provide enough detail to make the case.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: Re: Query regarding latest idea discussion for GSOC '13
parts:
I'll add that Claudia Beleites and I when were were admins for 2011
presented a short talk about GSOC-R at UseR!2011 in Warwick where we
made a point that student initiated projects should be welcomed and
supported. If you are a student with an idea, do post it and do ask for
mentoring and support. Some ideas are initially presented in a way that
doesn't excite folk, but a bit of rework can get them funded.

JN
